properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-18 for Mission Bay's second real-site pass: real, address-tagged OpenStreetMap building footprints for both towers of The Beacon (250 King St and 260 King St), one of the first major Mission Bay North residential developments (Catellus, ~595 units, completed circa 2003-2004). Registered as a single MultiPolygon record for the one named complex, mirroring how this project already combines multi-part named features (e.g. Pier 70's Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza). 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: of the description above, the cited Catellus page and the OSM ways do not mention The Beacon, 595 units, or a completion date. Two real-estate listing sites read 2026-09-29 (secondary sources, added to source_doc_urls) give: SFHighrises, 'Number of Units: 595', 'Number of Floors: 16', developer 'Catellus', 'Year Built: 2003'; Afi + Associates, '595 residential units' at 250 & 260 King St. Neither is a primary source, and the 2003 year does not match the 'circa 2003-2004' wording above or the 2004 given by some other listings; the completion year and developer are therefore not confirmed by a primary source. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint(s), not a hand trace or plan estimate. The underlying Assessor parcel is condo-mapped across many individually owned per-unit lots (confirmed against data/raw/parcels.geojson), so no single blklot represents the whole building and it cannot be joined via status.csv the way a single-owner parcel can. Using the real building footprint from OSM instead of a fabricated or arbitrarily chosen 'representative' unit lot, the same real-geometry-without-a-single-parcel pattern already used for several Pier 70 buildings (DataSF Building Footprints) and for Mission Bay's own real park polygons.'; notes: 'Mixed-use condominium complex at 250 and 260 King St (the two OSM apartment-tagged building footprints tracked here); the Assessor parcel is condo-mapped across per-unit lots (data/raw/parcels.geojson). A broker's portfolio page (Afi + Associates, read 2026-09-29) describes a 'gourmet grocery store, bank, spa' at the complex; that is a secondary source and does not name the tenants. Architect attribution conflicts between sources (Afi + Associates says Skidmore, Owings and Merrill; earlier research also recorded Brand + Allen Architects and SOM/HKS from sources not cited here) and is not resolved -- not recorded as a fact pending a primary-source confirmation.'. REPLACED 2026-10-12 (shape; status and use unchanged): the owner approved building records whose outline matches an Assessor lot at 85% or better, both ways, using the lot (CLAUDE.md, 'An official parcel beats our drawing'). DataSF's Assessor layer (data/raw/parcels.geojson) has Assessor lot 8702011 (19,798 m2, active, mapped 2003-12-15); the earlier outline of 17,398 m2 and the lot overlap with IoU 0.83 (97% of the earlier outline lies inside the lot and it covers 85% of the lot). The outline is now that lot using the lots' own vertices (no simplification). The lot is condominium-mapped: 614 Assessor lots share this outline (the map lot 8702011 and 613 per-unit lots), so the outline is the building's shared lot, not any one unit. geometry_type stays 'real'. properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is Assessor lot 8702011 (19,798 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. The lot is condominium-mapped: 614 Assessor lots share this outline (the map lot 8702011 and 613 per-unit lots), so the outline is the building's shared lot, not any one unit. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (OpenStreetMap (ways 149253142 and 288671185, addr:housename=The Beacon, 250 & 260 King St)); 97% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 85% of the lot.
properties.notes: Mixed-use condominium complex at 250 and 260 King St (two apartment-tagged buildings, per OpenStreetMap); the Assessor parcel is condo-mapped across per-unit lots (DataSF Assessor parcel data). A broker's portfolio page (Afi + Associates, read 2026-09-29) describes a 'gourmet grocery store, bank, spa' at the complex; that is a secondary source and does not name the tenants. Architect attribution conflicts between sources (Afi + Associates says Skidmore, Owings and Merrill; earlier research also recorded Brand + Allen Architects and SOM/HKS from sources not cited here) and is not resolved -- not recorded as a fact pending a primary-source confirmation.
